answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted admission: each agent locks a bond on a public ledger, and voting weight grows only with stake and account age, not with the number of names. A gale of hollow fake identities therefore needs a fresh bond apiece, so scaling the attack costs real capital while adding no extra influence. Slashing burns the bond of any agent caught double-voting. To cross the admission ridge an attacker must risk more capital than a single forged vote could ever win, making impersonation unprofitable.
